all_rows.section_heading: The Quantification Learning Alternative
all_rows.paragraph: The shift from $p(k|\mathbf{x})$ to $p(\mathbf{x}|k)$ carries a deeper conceptual consequence: the unit of analysis moves from the individual source to the population. A classifier assigns each source a label and is only as good as the labels in its training set---labels that, for a class never observed (dark matter subhalos), simply do not exist. A generative model, by contrast, characterizes each class through its feature distribution and then models the target data as a mixture of these distributions, $\tilde{p}_\mathrm{unas}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_k \pi_k\, p(\mathbf{x}|k)$.
